facts.statement: Savannasaurus lived during the Cenomanian to Lower Turonian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cenomanian–Lower Turonian, ~

facts.statement: Savannasaurus is a sauropod dinosaur found in the Late Cretaceous Winton Formation of Queensland, Australia.
facts.quote: Savannasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Winton Formation of Queensland, Australia.

facts.statement: The only known species, Savannasaurus elliottorum, was named in 2016 by Stephen Poropat and colleagues.
facts.quote: It contains one species, Savannasaurus elliottorum, named in 2016 by Stephen Poropat and colleagues.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, nicknamed "Wade", is the most complete Australian sauropod known and is housed at the Australian Age of Dinosaurs museum.
facts.quote: The holotype and only known specimen, originally nicknamed "Wade", is the most complete specimen of an Australian sauropod, and is held at the Australian Age of Dinosaurs museum.

facts.statement: The first Savannasaurus specimen was discovered in March 2005 by David Elliot and his family.
facts.quote: In March 2005, the first specimen of Savannasaurus was discovered by David Elliot, founder of Australian Age of Dinosaurs (AODF), along with his wife Judy and their children.

facts.statement: Preparing the Savannasaurus specimen took approximately ten years using air scribes and micro-jacks.
facts.quote: Preparation of the specimen took around a decade, with air scribes and micro-jacks being used.

facts.statement: The Savannasaurus holotype consists of approximately 40 bones.
facts.quote: AODF 660 consists of around 40 bones

facts.statement: The bones of the Savannasaurus holotype were preserved within an area of less than 20 square meters.
facts.quote: The bones were preserved over an area of less than 20 sqm.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the fifth dorsal vertebra and both humeri were trampled by other dinosaurs before fossilization.
facts.quote: The fifth dorsal vertebra and both humeri show signs of being trampled by other dinosaurs before fossilization

facts.statement: The genus name Savannasaurus is derived from the Taíno word zavana, meaning savanna, referencing its habitat.
facts.quote: the generic name of Savannasaurus, from Taíno zavana (the root of the word "savanna"), refers to the environment in which it was found

facts.statement: The species name elliottorum honors the Elliott family for their contributions to Australian paleontology.
facts.quote: the specific name elliottorum honours the Elliott family and their contributions to Australian palaeontology.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus was a medium-sized titanosaur measuring about 15 meters in length.
facts.quote: At 15 m long, Savannasaurus was a medium-sized titanosaur.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus had notably wide hips, reaching over 1.1 meters at their widest point.
facts.quote: It is notable for its wide hips, which would have been over 1.1 m wide at their widest points.

facts.statement: Wide hips and a flexible spine likely helped Savannasaurus navigate the muddy floodplains of its habitat.
facts.quote: Combined with a flexible vertebral column, these traits would have made Savannasaurus better at navigating the muddy ground of the floodplains that it lived on.

facts.statement: Analyses suggest Savannasaurus ancestors migrated to Australia via Antarctica approximately 105 to 100 million years ago.
facts.quote: Palaeobiogeographic analyses suggest that the ancestors of Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus were from either Asia or one of the southern Gondwanan continents; regardless, they likely migrated to Australia through Antarctica around 105–100 million years ago.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus is classified as a basal member of the Titanosauria but not part of the specialized Lithostrotia group.
facts.quote: Various traits suggest that Savannasaurus was an early-diverging (or basal) member of the Titanosauria, but not a member of the more specialized group Lithostrotia.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus weighed around 20 tons and stood approximately 3 meters at the shoulder.
facts.quote: Savannasaurus was a medium-sized titanosaur that measured about 15 m in length, with a weight of around 20 t and a shoulder height of around 3 m.

facts.statement: Poropat and colleagues suggested the undulating surface of a caudal vertebra as a distinguishing characteristic of Savannasaurus.
facts.quote: Poropat and colleagues suggested this as a distinguishing characteristic of Savannasaurus

facts.statement: The other caudal vertebrae were amphicoelous, having centra concave on both ends, a trait rare among titanosaurs except in Baotianmansaurus and Dongyangosaurus.
facts.quote: The other caudals were amphicoelous, or having centra that are concave on both ends, which was also rare among titanosaurs save for Baotianmansaurus and Dongyangosaurus

facts.statement: A well-developed longitudinal fossa extended for nearly the entire length along the side of the known cervical vertebra.
facts.quote: There was a well-developed longitudinal fossa, or excavation, along the side of the vertebra that extends for nearly its entire length

facts.statement: The laminae in the dorsal vertebrae were bilaterally asymmetric, with the left side better reinforced by extra laminae.
facts.quote: Notably, the laminae in the dorsals of Savannasaurus were bilaterally asymmetric; the left side of the vertebrae would have been better reinforced by extra laminae

facts.statement: The sternal plates lacked the long ridges present on the bottom surfaces of most Neosauropoda.
facts.quote: Second, they lacked the long ridges that were present on the bottom surfaces among most members of Neosauropoda

facts.statement: In Savannasaurus, the sternal plates were approximately 71% as long as the humeri.
facts.quote: In Savannasaurus, the ratio was approximately 71%

facts.statement: The third metacarpal was 49% the length of the radius.
facts.quote: The third metacarpal was 49% the length of the radius

facts.statement: These proportions made Savannasaurus extremely wide-hipped, a trait surpassed only by Opisthocoelicaudia and saltasaurines like Neuquensaurus.
facts.quote: Although titanosaurs were wide-bodied in general, these proportions made Savannasaurus extremely wide-hipped, surpassed only by Opisthocoelicaudia and saltasaurines such as Neuquensaurus

facts.statement: The ischium's articulation on the pubis was 56% as high as the bone was long, which is higher than in most titanosaurs.
facts.quote: The ischium's articulation on the pubis was 56% as high as the bone was long, higher than most titanosaurs

facts.statement: On the ischium, the iliac peduncle was only 32% of the bone's length, which is lower than in most other sauropods.
facts.quote: On the ischium, the iliac peduncle, one of the processes surrounding the acetabulum (hip joint), was only 32% of the bone's length, lower than most other sauropods

facts.statement: The front end of the ischium was 49% as wide as the bone was long, a ratio only similarly high in Diamantinasaurus (51%).
facts.quote: Furthermore, the front end of the ischium was 49% as wide as the bone was long; only Diamantinasaurus had a similarly high ratio (51%)

facts.statement: Mannion and colleagues found Savannasaurus within Saltasauridae in 2019 only when using equal weighting of characteristics, not implied weighting.
facts.quote: In their 2019 redescription of Jiangshanosaurus and Dongyanosaurus, Mannion and colleagues found both Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus inside Saltasauridae by equally weighting characteristics in their dataset, but using implied weighting eliminated this result.

facts.statement: Palaeobiogeographic analysis suggests the ancestors of Savannasaurus were likely Asian.
facts.quote: Using the modern geography of the continents, they found that the ancestors of the Australian sauropods Savannasaurus, Diamantinasaurus, and Wintonotitan were likely Asian.

facts.statement: Models incorporating Cretaceous geography suggest Savannasaurus ancestors had ranges spanning South America, Africa, and Indo-Madagascar.
facts.quote: Incorporating Cretaceous geography suggested ancestral ranges also spanning the Gondwanan continents of South America, Africa, and Indo-Madagascar.

facts.statement: During the Aptian to early Albian epochs, the region of Australia where Savannasaurus later lived was at 70°S latitude with a cool, temperate climate.
facts.quote: In the Aptian to early Albian epochs, this region of Australia would have been situated at a latitude of 70°S, with a cool, temperate climate.

facts.statement: Poropat and colleagues suggested that climate preferences might explain why Australian dinosaurs like Savannasaurus show affinities with Laurasian species.
facts.quote: Poropat and colleagues suggested that climate preferences could also explain the Laurasian affinities of Australian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus was named in 2016 by Poropat and colleagues.
facts.quote: fue nombrada en 2016 por Poropat et al.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Savannasaurus was originally nicknamed "Wade".
facts.quote: El único espécimen conocido fue apodado originalmente "Wade".

facts.statement: Remains of Savannasaurus were found in Queensland, Australia.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en Queensland

facts.statement: Savannasaurus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 94 million years ago in the Turonian stage.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 94 millones de años durante el Turoniense

facts.statement: Savannasaurus is notable for its wide hips, which would have been over 1.1 meters wide at their widest points.
facts.quote: Es notable por sus anchas caderas, que habrían tenido más de 1,1 metros de ancho en sus puntos más anchos.

facts.statement: A flexible spine combined with wide hips and robust limbs likely helped Savannasaurus navigate the muddy floodplains where it lived.
facts.quote: Combinados con una columna vertebral flexible, estos rasgos habrían hecho que Savannasaurus navegara mejor por el suelo fangoso de las llanuras aluviales en las que vivía.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus is classified as a basal member of Titanosauria that diverged early, rather than belonging to the specialized group Lithostrotia.
facts.quote: Varios rasgos sugieren que Savannasaurus era un miembro de Titanosauria que divergió temprano o basal, pero no un miembro del grupo más especializado Lithostrotia.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus was likely a "wide-gauge" sauropod, standing and walking with its feet far apart from its midline.
facts.quote: Like all titanosaurs, Savannasaurus was likely a "wide-gauge" sauropod, meaning that it would have stood and walked with its feet far apart from the midline.

facts.statement: The robust humerus of Savannasaurus is considered a likely adaptation to its wide-gauge stance.
facts.quote: The robust humerus of Savannasaurus was also considered a likely adaptation to a wide-gauge stance

facts.statement: Savannasaurus possessed traits that increased vertebral column flexibility, specifically the absence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations and prominent excavations below the transprezygapophyseal laminae.
facts.quote: Yet, Poropat and colleagues also noted traits that would have increased the flexibility of the vertebral column, namely the absence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations and the presence of prominent excavations (the centroprezygapophyseal fossae) below the transprezygapophyseal laminae.

facts.statement: The rock unit containing Savannasaurus fossils, the upper Winton Formation, is dated to about 93.9 million years ago at the Cenomanian-Turonian boundary.
facts.quote: The Belmont sheep station is part of the fossil-bearing rock units in the upper Winton Formation, which has been dated to around or just after the boundary between the Cenomanian and Turonian epochs of the Cretaceous—about 93.9 million years ago—based on uranium-lead dating of detrital zircons.

facts.statement: During the Cenomanian and Turonian, the area where Savannasaurus lived was located at a latitude of around 50°S.
facts.quote: During the Cenomanian and Turonian, the Winton area had a latitude of around 50°S.

facts.statement: A tooth of the theropod Australovenator found near the Savannasaurus holotype suggests that Australovenator may have fed on the specimen, causing its disarticulation.
facts.quote: A tooth belonging to Australovenator was found near the Savannasaurus holotype, suggesting that its feeding was responsible for the specimen's disarticulation.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the specific vertebral traits of Savannasaurus, such as the absence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations, were unique adaptations or shared features with Diamantinasaurus.
facts.quote: Yet, Poropat and colleagues also noted traits that would have increased the flexibility of the vertebral column, namely the absence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations and the presence of prominent excavations (the centroprezygapophyseal fossae) below the transprezygapophyseal laminae. Both of these were shared with Diamantinasaurus, but were otherwise rare among sauropods.

facts.statement: The genus Savannasaurus was established by Poropat et al. in 2016.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Poropat et al., 2016

facts.statement: The species Savannasaurus elliottorum was described by Poropat et al. in 2016.
facts.quote: species_authority: Poropat et al., 2016

facts.statement: Savannasaurus was a medium-sized sauropod dinosaur reaching approximately 15 meters in length.
facts.quote: Savannasaurus es un titanosaurio de tamaño mediano, con cerca de 15 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus had an unusually wide body, with its fused sacrum and ischium-pubis structure measuring nearly one meter at its narrowest points.
facts.quote: El sacro y la estructura fusionada del isquion y el pubis tienen cerca de un metro de ancho en sus puntos más estrechos, lo que hace a Savannasaurus un titanosauriano con un cuerpo inusualmente ancho.

facts.statement: The distal end of the fourth metacarpal in Savannasaurus was shaped like an hourglass.
facts.quote: el extremo del cuarto metacarpiano tiene forma de reloj de arena.

facts.statement: The astragalus of Savannasaurus was longer than it was wide or tall.
facts.quote: la longitud del astrágalo es mayor que su ancho o alto.

facts.statement: The internal structure of Savannasaurus vertebrae was pneumatized and filled with air due to small holes or chambers, and the dorsal ribs also possessed pneumatic cavities.
facts.quote: la estructura interna de las vértebras está neumatizada, llena de aire, gracias a varios pequeños agujeros o cámaras, y las costillas dorsales también poseen cavidades neumáticas.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus possessed opisthocoelous cervical and dorsal vertebrae and amphicoelous caudal vertebrae, a combination different from most titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales y dorsales conocidas son opistocelas, mientras que todas las vértebras caudales son anficelosas, a diferencia de la mayoría de los titanosaurios.

facts.statement: Unusually, the front articular surface of one of the caudal centra in Savannasaurus was wavy, concave in the upper half and convex in the lower half.
facts.quote: Inusualmente, la superficie de articulación frontal de uno de los centros caudales era ondulada, siendo cóncava en la mitad superior y convexa en la mitad inferior.

facts.statement: In Savannasaurus, the parapophysis, one of the rib articulations, was restricted to the front half of the centrum, unlike many specialized titanosaurs.
facts.quote: la parapófisis, una de las articulaciones de las costillas, estaba restringida a la mitad frontal del centro.

facts.statement: The dorsal laminae of Savannasaurus were bilaterally asymmetrical, with the left side of the vertebrae likely reinforced better by additional laminae.
facts.quote: las láminas de las dorsales de Savannasaurus eran asimétricas bilateralmente, el lado izquierdo de las vértebras se habría reforzado mejor con láminas adicionales.

facts.statement: The dorsal neural spines in Savannasaurus increased in height toward the posterior dorsals, did not split into two, and were taller than their corresponding articular surfaces.
facts.quote: las espinas neurales dorsales en la parte superior del centro aumentaron en altura hacia las dorsales posteriores, no se dividieron en dos y eran más altas que sus superficies articulares correspondientes.

facts.statement: In Savannasaurus, the sternal plates were approximately 71% of the length of the humerus.
facts.quote: En Savannasaurus , la proporción fue de aproximadamente el 71%.

facts.statement: The glenoid fossa articulating with the humerus in Savannasaurus was much larger than that of Diamantinasaurus.
facts.quote: la fosa glenoidea que se articulaba con el húmero era mucho más grande que la de Diamantinasaurus.

facts.statement: Unlike most titanosauriforms, the articulation with the scapula at the rear of the coracoid in Savannasaurus was higher than the entire bone from front to back.
facts.quote: A diferencia de la mayoría de los titanosauriformes, salvo Daxiatitan, Ligabuesaurus y Sauroposeidon, la articulación con la escápula en la parte posterior del hueso era más alta que todo el hueso de adelante hacia atrás.

facts.statement: The radius of Savannasaurus was twisted around its axis with the long axes of the two ends oriented in different planes, a feature seen only in Huabeisaurus, Epachthosaurus, and Rapetosaurus.
facts.quote: El radio estaba torcido alrededor de su eje, con los ejes largos de los dos extremos orientados en diferentes planos, visto de otra manera solo en Huabeisaurus, Epachthosaurus y Rapetosaurus.

facts.statement: The maximum width of the upper end of the radius in Savannasaurus was 33% of the bone's length, and it featured a strong crest at the outer rear corner called the interosseous crest.
facts.quote: El ancho máximo de su extremo superior, 33% de la longitud del hueso y la presencia de una fuerte cresta en la esquina exterior trasera, la cresta interósea, fueron más típicas.

facts.statement: Like Diamantinasaurus and Wintonotitan, the third metacarpals were the longest in Savannasaurus, followed by the second, first, fourth, and fifth.
facts.quote: Como Diamantinasaurus y Wintonotitan, los terceros metacarpianos fueron los más largos, seguidos por el segundo, primero, cuarto y quinto.

facts.statement: The third metacarpal in Savannasaurus was 49% of the radius length, which was short for a sauropod but at least 45% as long as in all macronarians.
facts.quote: El tercer metacarpiano tenía el 49% de la longitud del radio, que era corto para un titanosauriano, pero era al menos el 45% como en todos los macronarios.

facts.statement: A distinctive feature of Savannasaurus was that the lower part of the fourth metacarpal was hourglass-shaped, not trapezoidal or hexagonal.
facts.quote: Una característica distintiva es que la parte inferior del cuarto metacarpiano tenía forma de reloj de arena, no trapezoidal ni hexagonal.

facts.statement: The presence of phalanges in Savannasaurus was unusual, as all titanosaurs except Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus had hands formed only by metacarpals.
facts.quote: La presencia de falanges es inusual; todos los titanosaurianos excepto Savannasaurus y Diamantinasaurus tenían manos formadas solo por metacarpianos.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus was likely a sauropod with a "wide-bodied" posture, meaning it stood and walked with its feet very far apart from the midline.
facts.quote: Como todos los titanosaurianos, Savannasaurus era probablemente un saurópodo de "cuerpo ancho", lo que significa que se habría parado y caminado con los pies muy separados de la línea media.

facts.statement: In 2020, Poropat and colleagues pointed to the width of its sternal and sacral plates as evidence of a wide-gauge posture.
facts.quote: En 2020, Poropat y sus colegas señalaron el ancho de sus placas esternal y sacro como evidencia de una postura de amplio calibre.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested the unusual shape of the astragalus was an adaptation for weight-bearing, but the absence of other hind limb bones left this unclear.
facts.quote: También sugirieron que la forma inusual del astrágalo también era una adaptación a la carga de peso, pero la ausencia de otros huesos de las extremidades posteriores no aclaraba esto.

facts.statement: Poropat and colleagues observed traits that would have increased spinal flexibility, specifically the absence of hypheno-hipantrous articulations and the presence of prominent excavations, the centroprezygapophyseal fossae, below the transprezygapophyseal laminae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Poropat y sus colegas también observaron rasgos que habrían aumentado la flexibilidad de la columna vertebral, a saber, la ausencia de articulaciones hipofeno-hipántro y la presencia de excavaciones prominentes , las fosas centroprezygapofisarias, debajo de las láminas transprezygapofisarias.

facts.statement: Poropat and colleagues observed that both Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus likely lived in an alluvial plain with clay-rich soil and high rainfall, implying the ground would occasionally become muddy and dangerous for large sauropods.
facts.quote: Poropat y sus colegas observaron que tanto Savannasaurus como Diamantinasaurus habrían vivido en una llanura aluvial con suelo rico en arcilla y altas precipitaciones, lo que implicaría que el suelo ocasionalmente se volvería fangoso y peligroso para los grandes saurópodos.

facts.statement: Researchers considered it possible that environmental pressures selected individuals capable of navigating muddy terrain, and that Savannasaurus may have spent more time near water than other sauropods.
facts.quote: Consideraron posible que las presiones ambientales hubieran seleccionado a individuos capaces de navegar por terrenos fangosos, y que Savannasaurus podría haber pasado más tiempo cerca del agua que otros saurópodos.

facts.statement: Flexible vertebrae to escape swamps, barrel-shaped bodies similar to hippos, a wide-gauge posture, and robust forelimbs to distribute body weight would have been useful for this niche.
facts.quote: Vértebras flexibles, para escapar de los pantanos , cuerpos en forma de barril similares a los de los hipopótamos, la postura de gran calibre y las extremidades anteriores robustas, todo para distribuir su peso corporal, habrían sido útiles para tal nicho.

facts.statement: Researchers postulated that saltasaurines may have been subject to similar selective pressures, so the "typical" titanosaurian body plan may have been acquired convergently several times.
facts.quote: Postularon que los saltasaurinos podrían haber estado sujetos a presiones selectivas similares, por lo que el plan corporal de titanosáurido "típico" puede haber sido adquirido de manera convergente varias veces.

facts.statement: While the environment might have selected for longer necks to access water, Poropat and colleagues observed that Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus likely had relatively short necks, though overlapping cervical ribs may have improved stability in Savannasaurus.
facts.quote: Si bien el mismo entorno también podría haber seleccionado cuellos más largos para proporcionar un acceso más fácil al agua, Poropat y sus colegas observaron que Savannasaurus y Diamantinasaurus probablemente tenían cuellos relativamente cortos, aunque las costillas cervicales superpuestas podrían haber mejorado la estabilidad en Savannasaurus.

facts.quote: Parent group: Diamantinasauria

facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3
